units.source_text: 在雷鸣般的掌声中，库拉巴喀向我们施了一礼，安静的走向钢琴，接着轻松自在地弹起了他自己作词作曲的抒情诗。

en.t: Amid thunderous applause, Kurabaka bowed to us, walked quietly to the piano, and then began lightly and effortlessly to play the lyric poem for which he had written both the words and the music.

units.source_text: 根据托喀的说法，库拉巴喀是河童国有史以来“前无古人，后无来者”的天才音乐家。

en.t: According to Tok, Kurabaka was a genius musician unmatched before or since in the whole history of the country of the kappas.

units.source_text: 吸引我的不仅是库拉巴喀的音乐，还有他的另一个特长——抒情诗，因此我无比认真的倾听钢琴弹奏出的宛转悦耳的旋律。

en.t: What drew me in was not only Kurabaka's music but also his other gift, lyric poetry, so I listened with the utmost seriousness to the graceful, beautiful melody flowing from the piano.

units.source_text: 托喀和马咯恐怕甚至比我还要沉醉其中。

en.t: Tok and Maro were probably even more entranced by it than I was.

units.source_text: 唯独托喀的那只美丽的（以河童们的审美来说）雌河童却紧紧捏着节目单，不断烦躁地吐出长长的舌头。

en.t: Only Tok's beautiful female kappa, beautiful by kappa standards, clutched the program tightly and kept irritably sticking out her long tongue.

units.source_text: 听马咯提过，十来年前她曾经想捉库拉巴喀而没有捉住，因此直到现在还把这位音乐家看作眼中钉肉中刺呢。

en.t: Maro had told me that about ten years earlier she had tried to catch Kurabaka but failed, and for that reason she still regarded this musician as a thorn in her side.
